title: Dominic and the Deadline
premise: Astrid Marchetti has spent a decade as a whistle-blower shuffled through four identities by a witness-protection apparatus that keeps rewriting its own rules. When her dead handler's calendar sends her a meeting invitation set for tomorrow, she realizes his death was staged and his silence was bought. The meeting pulls her into an extraction operation targeting Marek Vos, a defector carrying proof that the protection program itself launders the very corruption Astrid exposed — and Marek may be bait to flush out every protected witness at once. Astrid must choose between the rules that kept her alive and the man she's ordered to abandon, and in the end she burns her own cover to expose the program, trading her anonymity for justice and discovering that the handler's invitation was his posthumous act of love.
about_author: Elodie Lockridge is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent six years inside financial institutions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped between systems and conscience, and she lives under a name she chose herself.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Astrid Marchetti, living as 'Nadia Kessler' in a Rotterdam suburb, receives a calendar invite from handler Elias Brandt — killed eight months ago. POV Astrid. The beat is dread sharpened into curiosity: rules say report it, but the reporting channel bounces to an address that doesn't exist.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: Astrid reviews her decade of relocations, each name shedding a life, and tests the invitation against her protocols. POV Astrid, with a flashback to Brandt recruiting her. Emotional beat: exhaustion with a protection that feels increasingly like captivity.

chapters.title: Tomorrow, 09:00
chapters.summary: She decides to attend, leaving dead-man switches in three places. POV Astrid, plus a brief interlude from an unnamed watcher who reports her movement. The beat is cold resolve — she goes not from trust but because the rules have failed her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Brandt
chapters.summary: At the meeting, a stranger claiming to be Brandt's successor, Calloway, briefs her: a defector, Marek Vos, holds files proving the protection program launders corruption — her own case files. POV Astrid. Beat: vertigo, as the system that saved her is the crime.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Astrid verifies fragments of Vos's claims and finds her old case numbers redacted inside program archives she can still access. POV Astrid. Emotional beat: grief curdling into anger — ten years of sacrifice for an institution eating its own witnesses.

chapters.title: The Defector in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Calloway shows her Vos: young, frightened, holding a drive. Astrid notices the photo's metadata is doctored. POV Astrid. Beat: first real doubt — is Vos a defector or bait? Her handler instincts wake fully.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching Nadia Kessler
chapters.summary: Astrid returns to find her apartment searched with professional subtlety. POV Astrid, alternating with the watcher, revealed as a program auditor named Ilsa Rehn tracking 'leak vectors.' Beat: paranoia becomes physical; the walls are closing.

chapters.title: Brandt's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Following a cipher Brandt taught her, Astrid finds a hidden message: 'The meeting is the trap. The defector is the net. Trust the invitation, not the inviter.' POV Astrid with Brandt's voice through the dead drop. Beat: mourning and gratitude — he planned for his own death.

chapters.title: Extraction Orders
chapters.summary: Calloway orders Astrid to personally extract Vos from a Vienna safehouse in 48 hours, alone, off-book. POV Astrid. Emotional beat: the trap's shape becomes visible — they want her hands on him so she's implicated in whatever happens.

chapters.title: Vienna in the Rain
chapters.summary: Astrid travels dark, using a fifth name she's never dared use. POV Astrid. Beat: fragile freedom — for the first time in ten years, she moves without permission, and it feels like flying and falling at once.

chapters.title: The Safehouse and the Stranger
chapters.summary: Astrid reaches Vos, who doesn't act like bait — he's terrified, genuine, and recognizes her real name, which no one living should know. POV Astrid, then Vos. Beat: connection against instinct; he says Brandt promised him she'd come.

chapters.title: What Marek Carried
chapters.summary: Vos's drive contains ledgers showing witnesses' relocation funds routed through shell companies into the pockets of program directors. POV Vos, recounting his escape. Beat: the inheritance theme lands — he inherited his brother's evidence and his brother's death sentence.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Danube
chapters.summary: Extraction goes wrong; Calloway's team, not rescuers, hits the safehouse. Astrid and Vos escape through flood tunnels. POV Astrid. Beat: adrenaline and betrayal — the operation was always designed to end with both of them dead.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: Ilsa Rehn corners Astrid — but Ilsa isn't with the conspirators; she's been auditing the program for years and couldn't prove it without a witness. POV Ilsa. Beat: wary alliance; two women who live by rules deciding, together, to break them.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Astrid and Vos, hiding in a canal boat, grow close; he asks her real name and she gives it — her first freely chosen act in a decade. POV Astrid. Beat: tenderness under threat; love as the one thing she refuses to surrender again.

chapters.title: The Deadline Moves
chapters.summary: Calloway accelerates the timeline: the program will 'retire' all protected witnesses at a scheduled audit in 36 hours, erasing evidence and people together. POV Calloway, revealing his cold bureaucratic logic. Beat: horror at banality; the clock becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: Brandt's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Astrid decodes Brandt's final dead drop: a complete duplicate of Vos's evidence, plus a letter — he discovered the laundering, was killed for it, and left her the means to finish it. POV Astrid. Beat: the dead man's love letter is a case file; grief becomes fuel.

chapters.title: Breaking In
chapters.summary: Astrid, Vos, and Rehn infiltrate the program's Vienna archive during the audit to seed the evidence into official channels before the purge. POV alternating Astrid/Vos. Beat: taut competence; the hunted become the operators.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Trapped in the archive, Astrid faces Calloway, who offers her old life back — a new name, Vos erased — if she hands over the drive. POV Astrid. Beat: the thematic crux; she answers by pressing send, broadcasting the files to every press outlet and oversight body at once.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: The purge begins early; a running battle through the archive as Rehn buys time, is wounded, and survives; Vos is nearly taken. POV Vos. Beat: climax — everything Astrid built to protect herself is spent protecting someone else.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Dawn: the files are public, arrests begin, Calloway is taken by his own colleagues. Astrid stands in a courtyard as her four identities are formally dissolved. POV Astrid. Beat: catharsis — she is no one official now, which means she is finally herself.

chapters.title: A Name She Chose
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Astrid and Vos, under testimony protection and new names of their own choosing, visit Brandt's grave. She leaves the original invitation on the stone. POV Astrid. Beat: quiet resolution — the deadline passed, the love remained, and the inheritance was justice.
